title: Work head bounds across computation segments
statement: Let $k,N,B$ be natural numbers with $N>0$, let $Q$ be a state type, let $x$ be a Boolean input, let $M$ be a $k$-tape machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $(c_i)_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of configurations on $x$. Suppose that for every $i<N$ there is a time $u$ such that every configuration reached from $c_i$ at a time $v\le u$ has all work-tape head positions in $[-B,B]$, and at time $u$ the machine is either halted or $i+1<N$ and its configuration equals $c_{i+1}$. Then, at every time $t$, the run of $M$ from $c_0$ has all work-tape head positions in $[-B,B]$.
hypotheses_covered: For each $i<N$, there is a segment endpoint $u$
All heads stay in $[-B,B]$ through each segment endpoint
At each endpoint the run is halted or equals the next configuration, with $i+1<N$
